To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
water-soluble polymethacrylic acid comb polymers grafted to polyethylene glycol have a longer circulation time in the blood and a greater tumor accumulation than do the linear polymer counterparts.

water-soluble, cyclic, comb polymer conjugates of polyethylene glycol and poly(acrylic acid), which are topologically similar to dendrimers, show greatly extended circulation in vivo compared to their linear polymer counterparts and are promising drug delivery vehicles.
cyclic polymers show a greater area under serum concentration versus time curves and longer half-life times in the blood compared to linear polymers of similar molecular weight.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new synthetic methodologies for the preparation of well-defined water-soluble polymethacrylate-based comb polymers and the study of their physico-chemical and biological properties.
the synthesis of novel polymer architectures and their application in biomedical research.
the development of new polymer architectures for use as drug delivery carriers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the longer the circulation time, the more tumor accumulation.

the pharmacokinetic profile of a water-soluble polymer depends on its molecular weight, chain stiffness, chain ends, and branching, and that cyclic polymers are superior to linear polymers in terms of pharmacokinetic profile.
the pharmacokinetic properties of water-soluble polymethacrylate comb polymers are strongly influenced by molecular weight, number of chain termini and branching, but not by chain flexibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyclic comb polymers have a longer circulation time than their linear counterparts, and that the longer circulation time is associated with a greater tumor accumulation.
cyclic polymer architecture is an important feature for the design of polymer therapeutics.

the pharmacokinetics of a polymer are influenced by its topology, and in the case of cyclic versus linear PEGylates, the cyclic polymer has a longer circulation half-life, a greater area under serum concentration versus time curves and greater tumor accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polymer topology can be used as a tool to tune the pharmacokinetic properties of a given polymer.
the polymer topology can be used to modulate the polymer pharmacokinetic profile and thus its tissue distribution.
the pharmacokinetic properties of a polymer can be tuned by altering its topology, in this case from linear to cyclic.
